title: Shattered Compositionality: Counterintuitive Learning Dynamics of Transformers for Arithmetic
abstract: arXiv:2601.22510v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) often achieve strong benchmark accuracy yet remain brittle under small distribution shifts. While recent mechanistic studies reveal the discrepancy between LLMs and humans in skill compositions, the learning dynamics of skill acquisition and the role of data distributions remain elusive. In this study, we train transformers on synthetic arithmetic tasks with black-box model-agnostic metrics for analyzing non-human skill compositions. We discover that transformers often acquire skills for arithmetic in reverse order or in parallel instead of human-like sequential rules--a phenomenon we refer to as shattered compositionality. To explain these behaviors, we provide evidence that correlational matching to the training data, rather than causal or procedural composition, shapes learning dynamics. translated_title: 破碎的组合性：Transformer 在算术任务上反直觉的学习动态
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLMs）通常能在基准测试中取得很高的准确率，但在微小的分布偏移下却表现脆弱。尽管近期的机制可解释性研究揭示了 LLMs 与人类在技能组合方式上的差异，但技能习得的学习动态以及数据分布在其中所起的作用仍不明确。在本研究中，我们在合成算术任务上训练 Transformer，并采用黑盒、模型无关的指标来分析非人类式的技能组合。我们发现，Transformer 在习得算术技能时往往遵循与人类相反的顺序，或者以并行的方式获取技能，而不是像人类那样按顺序逐步掌握规则——我们将这种现象称为“破碎的组合性”。为了解释这些行为，我们提供了证据表明，塑造学习动态的是对训练数据的相关性匹配，而非因果性或程序性的组合。由此，这种非人类式的技能习得方式会在部分习得的技能之间产生竞争（原文摘要在此处截断）。
tldr: 该研究提出了“破碎的组合性”现象，发现 Transformer 在算术任务上以反直觉的并行或倒序方式习得技能，并证明这种学习动态源于对训练数据的相关性匹配而非因果或程序性组合。
en_tdlr: This study reveals "shattered compositionality"—transformers acquire arithmetic skills in reverse or parallel order rather than human-like sequences—and shows that correlational matching to training data, not causal or procedural composition, drives these counterintuitive learning dynamics.
